scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
administering_body: National Health Authority (NHA), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
target_beneficiaries: Bottom ~40% economically vulnerable families identified per SECC 2011 deprivation/occupational criteria (state-specific extensions vary); since Sept 2024, all senior citizens aged 70+ regardless of income (Vay Vandana top-up)
coverage_amount_summary: Rs 5 lakh per family per year, family floater, cashless and paperless; additional Rs 5 lakh top-up cover for citizens aged 70+ (separate from family cover), approved by Union Cabinet Sept 2024
empanelled_hospitals_summary: ~36,229 empanelled hospitals nationwide as of Feb 2026 per secondary sources citing NHA dashboard data (approx. 19,483 government/public facilities + 16,746 private hospitals; up from approx. 27,000 in 2023); network size fluctuates continuously, treat as approximate
data_source: WebSearch aggregation (NHA/MoHFW press material summarized by secondary sources; no direct .gov.in fetch this session)
notes: Largest govt-funded health assurance scheme globally by beneficiary count. Operates in convergence with several state schemes (see Telangana and Andhra Pradesh rows) rather than replacing them. Exact current empanelled-hospital count and beneficiary-family count should be re-verified against the live NHA dashboard when direct fetch is possible. RC2 UPDATE (2026-07-22): West Bengal became the 36th and final State/UT to adopt AB PM-JAY -- approved at the new BJP state government's first cabinet meeting (11 May 2026) and rolled out from 1 July 2026, reportedly benefiting approx. 1.43 crore approved families there (West Bengal's prior TMC government had declined to join the scheme for years). This completes nationwide State/UT-level coverage of PM-JAY, a significant milestone not captured in the RC1 pass. Empanelled-hospital figure also refreshed this session (see coverage_amount / empanelled_hospitals_summary fields) with a more specific, though still secondary-sourced, count.

administering_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (Directorate General of CGHS)
target_beneficiaries: Serving and retired central government employees and their dependent family members; also covers some autonomous body employees, MPs, ex-MPs, Members of specified categories, and journalists in certain cities per separate orders
coverage_amount_summary: No fixed monetary ceiling; cashless treatment at CGHS package rates covering OPD, IPD/hospitalization, diagnostics, and AYUSH systems; FY2025-26 CGHS budget reported at approx. Rs 2,370 crore
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Approx. 2,486 empanelled private hospitals/diagnostic centres plus all CGHS wellness centres and government hospitals across roughly 80 covered cities
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing MoHFW/CGHS material via secondary sources
notes: IMPORTANT DOMAIN CHANGE: legacy domains cghs.gov.in and cghs.nic.in were deactivated on 28 April 2025 when a new unified CGHS Digital Platform/HMIS went live; cghs.mohfw.gov.in is now the only current official portal. Beneficiary count cited in secondary sources ranges 42-50 lakh depending on source/date; treat exact figure as PENDING_VERIFICATION. RC2 UPDATE (2026-07-22): renewed search still found a spread (a Wikipedia-sourced figure of 47.44 lakh vs. other secondary sources rounding to 'around 50 lakh' or 'over 40 lakh'); no single authoritative current figure was resolved this session, so the beneficiary count is still best treated as an approximate range (approx. 42-50 lakh, with 47.44 lakh as the most specific individual figure found) rather than a settled number -- retained as a known gap rather than guessed. Other row facts (domain, package-rate cashless model, budget figure) re-corroborated across additional independent sources this session, supporting a modest confidence increase.

administering_body: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
target_beneficiaries: Employees earning up to Rs 21,000/month (Rs 25,000/month for persons with disabilities) in establishments with 10+ employees (varies by state) covered under the ESI Act, plus their dependents
coverage_amount_summary: No fixed ceiling on medical treatment cost (full medical care from day one of employment); cash benefits include sickness benefit at 70% of wages (up to 91 days/year, extendable up to 2 years at 80% for 34 specified long-term illnesses), disability benefit at ~90% of wages, and maternity benefit at 100% of wages; post-retirement/permanent-disability medical care continues for a nominal annual fee (reported ~Rs 120)
empanelled_hospitals_summary: ESI hospitals and dispensaries network across 668 notified districts (565 fully notified + 103 partially notified) in 36 states/UTs
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing ESIC official material via secondary sources
notes: Wage-ceiling and district-notification figures should be periodically re-checked as they are revised by government notification from time to time.

administering_body: Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence, Government of India (Central Organisation ECHS, headed by a Managing Director)
target_beneficiaries: Retired Armed Forces personnel (ex-servicemen) drawing pension, and their dependents (spouse, dependent unemployed/unmarried/divorced/widowed daughters, dependent sons up to 25 years, handicapped children, dependent parents)
coverage_amount_summary: Generally no fixed monetary ceiling on cost of treatment; covers OPD consultation, hospitalization, diagnostics, surgeries, medicines, and specialist care at no direct cost to the veteran; one-time contribution required at enrollment, broadly reported as ranging from approx. Rs 30,000 (JCOs/Other Ranks) up to approx. Rs 1.2 lakh (Officer ranks), per revised ECHS contribution rates -- a full rank-wise breakdown table was not located this session, so treat this two-tier range as indicative rather than exhaustive
empanelled_hospitals_summary: 427+ ECHS polyclinics plus service/military hospitals and empanelled civil/private hospitals nationwide
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing DESW/ECHS official material via secondary sources
notes: Scheme approved 30 Dec 2002, launched 1 Apr 2003. RC2 FILLED (2026-07-22): one-time contribution amount partially resolved -- multiple sources (including an Indian Navy 'Revised Rates of ECHS Contribution' circular) converge on a broad two-tier range of approx. Rs 30,000 for JCOs/Other Ranks up to approx. Rs 1.2 lakh for Officer ranks. This is a meaningful improvement over the RC1 'not independently verified' state, but a complete rank-by-rank table (covering all intermediate ranks) was not found; treat the figure as a directionally-correct range rather than an exhaustive schedule, and re-verify against the official ECHS rate table (echs.gov.in) when direct fetch access is available.

administering_body: Aarogyasri Health Care Trust, Health, Medical and Family Welfare Department, Government of Telangana
target_beneficiaries: Originally Below Poverty Line (BPL)/white-ration-card households; the Dec 2023 relaunch broadened intent toward wider population coverage, and in May 2025 the scheme was extended to orphans (full coverage without fresh means-testing); operates in convergence with AB PM-JAY
coverage_amount_summary: Rs 10 lakh per family per year (doubled from a prior Rs 5 lakh ceiling under the government formed in Dec 2023); in July 2024 the government added 163 new medical procedures to the package, of which 98 are funded/covered via AB-PMJAY convergence and 65 are state-funded
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Approx. 1,400+ empanelled government and private hospitals under Aarogyasri Health Care Trust across Telangana, covering approx. 1,835 medical/surgical procedures across 21+ specialties (the pre-existing 1,672-procedure list plus the 163 procedures added in July 2024); exact current hospital count fluctuates and should be treated as approximate
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing Telangana govt announcements via news and secondary sources
notes: RENAME/CHANGE FOUND: previously operated simply as 'Aarogyasri' (originally 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' at 2007 launch under undivided AP, later just 'Aarogyasri' in Telangana); the Congress-led government under CM A. Revanth Reddy (sworn in Dec 2023) relaunched it as 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' with the coverage increase to Rs 10 lakh, effective 9 Dec 2023. Distinct from the Telangana Employees Health Scheme/NEHS (see separate row), which covers only government employees/pensioners rather than the general BPL population. RC2 FILLED (2026-07-22): empanelled-hospital count refreshed to approx. 1,400+ hospitals (cross-corroborated across at least two independent secondary sources), with total procedure count of approx. 1,835 -- consistent with, and corroborating, the previously-recorded '1,672 + 163 new = 1,835' procedure math already in this row.

scheme_name: New Employees Health Scheme (NEHS) [formerly Employees Health Scheme / EHS Telangana]
administering_body: Employees Health Care Trust (EHCT), Government of Telangana (newly constituted trust headed by the Chief Secretary, with 17 government representatives, 10 employee representatives, and 3 pensioner representatives)
target_beneficiaries: Telangana state government employees, service pensioners, family pensioners, and their eligible dependent family members (reported ~17.88 lakh beneficiaries: ~4.39 lakh employees, ~3.62 lakh pensioners, ~9.88 lakh dependents)
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless treatment with no prescribed upper financial ceiling stated for approved treatment; 1,816 medical and surgical packages aligned with CGHS package rates
empanelled_hospitals_summary: 114 government hospitals plus 886 empanelled private hospitals and wellness centres, including major chains (Apollo, Yashoda, KIMS, Medicover, Kamineni, Continental, CARE, Star, Basavatarakam)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation of contemporaneous news coverage (launch-week reporting)
notes: VERY RECENT RENAME/RESTRUCTURE: NEHS was launched 17 July 2026 (four days before this collection date), replacing the earlier Employees Health Scheme (EHS) which had been administered via the Aarogyasri Health Care Trust's hospital network. A dedicated new Employees Health Care Trust (EHCT) now administers it, with a formal trust deed unveiled at launch. Because this change is only days old, corroboration is currently limited to launch-week news coverage rather than settled reference sources; confidence capped accordingly. Re-verify beneficiary/hospital counts and portal stability in a future collection cycle.

scheme_name: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Scheme [formerly Dr. YSR Aarogyasri]
administering_body: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (formally Dr. Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao Vaidya Seva Trust), Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, Government of Andhra Pradesh
target_beneficiaries: Below Poverty Line (BPL) families and families with annual income up to Rs 5 lakh in Andhra Pradesh
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless treatment up to Rs 25 lakh per eligible family per year: the first Rs 2.5 lakh of approved treatment cost is covered via an insurance company, with expenses beyond Rs 2.5 lakh up to Rs 25 lakh borne directly by the Trust; approx. 3,257 approved medical/surgical procedures across 31 super-speciality categories; scheme is integrated with AB PM-JAY
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Network of government hospitals plus approx. 782 of 785 designated private hospitals actively empanelled under the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust across Andhra Pradesh, per the Trust CEO's statement as of May 2026; the AP government released a further Rs 919.13 crore in May 2026 to clear outstanding dues owed to empanelled private hospitals, evidencing an actively-running (not dormant) network
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing AP govt/health department material via secondary sources
notes: CONFIRMED RENAME: this scheme has changed names repeatedly with changes of government - launched 2007 as 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' under YSR Congress founder Dr Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy; renamed 'NTR Aarogya Seva'/'NTR Vaidya Seva' under TDP (from 2014); renamed 'Dr. YSR Aarogyasri' in 2019 under YSRCP (CM Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy); renamed again to 'Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva' in July 2024 after the TDP-led NDA coalition (CM N. Chandrababu Naidu) took office. The administering trust was correspondingly renamed from 'Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust' to 'Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust'. The Rs 25 lakh coverage figure and Rs 2.5 lakh insurance-company threshold appear consistently across multiple secondary sources but were not confirmed against a primary .gov.in document this session; treat as high-confidence but not certainty. RC2 FILLED (2026-07-22): empanelled-hospital count refreshed with a specific, named-official figure (782 of 785 private hospitals, per the Trust CEO, May 2026) plus corroborating evidence of a May 2026 Rs 919.13 crore dues-clearance disbursement to those hospitals -- both facts sourced via medicaldialogues.in, a specialist health-news outlet, not merely a generic insurance aggregator.

administering_body: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (administering trust renamed July 2024 from Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust; scheme name 'EHS' itself was not renamed), Government of Andhra Pradesh
target_beneficiaries: Current and retired Andhra Pradesh state government employees and their dependent family members
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless inpatient and outpatient treatment, hospital stays, and follow-up/chronic-disease care, replacing the earlier medical-reimbursement process; RC2 FILLED (2026-07-22): coverage ceiling reported as Rs 2 lakh per episode of illness for the state government employee/pensioner/dependent beneficiary, per the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Medical Attendance (APIMA) Rules, 1972, with the number of covered episodes per beneficiary limited as per those Rules; figure cross-corroborated across multiple independent secondary/aggregator sources (Bajaj Finserv, Aditya Birla Capital, Acko), though still not confirmed against a primary .gov.in/G.O. document this session
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Network of empanelled hospitals shared with the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust network across Andhra Pradesh (exact current count not independently verified this session)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing secondary/aggregator sources; several aggregator sites still reference the pre-2024 trust name
notes: NAME NUANCE: unlike the BPL-facing scheme (Dr YSR Aarogyasri -> Dr NTR Vaidya Seva), the employee-facing 'EHS' scheme brand name itself does not appear to have changed in 2024; only its administering trust was renamed. Multiple aggregator/secondary sources have not updated to reflect the July 2024 trust rename and still say 'Dr YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust' - flagged here as a known lag in secondary sources, not necessarily a fact error. RC2 FILLED (2026-07-22): coverage ceiling of Rs 2 lakh per episode of illness (per APIMA Rules, 1972) is now recorded, resolving the RC1 PENDING_VERIFICATION gap, though still on secondary-source corroboration only; a direct G.O./ehs.ap.gov.in fetch remains the recommended final verification step.

scheme_name: Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) [includes the Health Minister's Cancer Patient Fund, HMCPF]
administering_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (Managing Committee / Technical Committee of the Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi)
target_beneficiaries: Patients from families living Below the Poverty Line (per the respective State/UT's BPL criteria) with annual family income not exceeding Rs 1,25,000, suffering from major life-threatening diseases, receiving treatment at listed Central Government hospitals, AIIMS/institutes of national importance, or identified state government super-speciality hospitals
coverage_amount_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs 15 lakh per patient for major life-threatening diseases (e.g. heart disease, kidney failure, liver disease); up to Rs 15 lakh under the Health Minister's Cancer Patient Fund (HMCPF) component for cancer treatment; up to Rs 20 lakh for identified rare diseases; funds are released as a grant-in-aid paid directly to the Medical Superintendent of the treating government hospital/institute rather than reimbursed to the patient or family
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Central Government hospitals, AIIMS and other institutes of national importance, and identified state government/regional super-speciality hospitals designated to receive RAN/HMCPF grants (a defined list maintained by MoHFW; this is a hospital-based grant-disbursement mechanism, not a private-hospital empanelment network of the PM-JAY/state-Aarogyasri type)
application_portal: Not a self-service beneficiary portal; application is routed through the Medical Superintendent of the treating government hospital/institute
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing MoHFW official material and secondary/aggregator sources
notes: NEW ROW added during RC2 enrichment (2026-07-22): genuine, currently active, national, MoHFW-administered financial-coverage-for-healthcare scheme not included in the RC1 pass. Established 13 January 1997 with an initial corpus contribution of Rs 5 crore from MoHFW. Distinct in mechanism from the insurance-style schemes elsewhere in this dataset: RAN pays a one-time grant to the treating hospital rather than providing a pre-defined annual per-family floater/sum-insured. The RC1 collection report excluded a superficially similar item (state Chief Minister's Relief Fund medical grants) as 'discretionary, case-by-case ex-gratia' aid; RAN was judged distinct and in-scope because it has defined eligibility (BPL status, family income ceiling of Rs 1,25,000/year) and defined coverage ceilings (Rs 15 lakh / Rs 15 lakh (HMCPF) / Rs 20 lakh across its three named components), i.e. it is a structured scheme rather than discretionary aid. Application/administration flows through the treating hospital's Medical Superintendent rather than a public beneficiary self-service portal; no dedicated online application tracker was identified. Confidence capped in the 82-88 band per this session's WebSearch-only methodology (no direct .gov.in fetch was possible, though a mohfw.gov.in FAQ PDF and the main.mohfw.gov.in scheme page were both cited consistently across independent search results).
